sourceTraceSupplement.text: Keyboard focus must remain visible. Opening an album or playlist from its focused tile starts the detail view at the top and focuses its Back control immediately, including while reads are loading or failed. Later data updates do not replay that focus move. Returning through sidebar navigation keeps its existing focus and saved detail scroll. A focused playlist Back returns to that exact playlist tile and reveals it, or to the list heading if the tile is unavailable. When removing a queue occurrence whose Remove button owns focus, move to the next visible Remove action, then the previous visible one, or Close queue if none remain. Skip collapsed Earlier history and reveal only the needed distance above the player; removing a repeated song must remove only that occurrence. Leave focus elsewhere untouched. In All songs, albums and playlists, keep the focused song row and its checkbox, artwork, title and actions clear of the sticky heading, selection toolbar, player and changing playback notices. Arrow navigation follows each key press, including quick repeats. Reveal only the needed distance; pointer selection and passive updates must not scroll the list or take focus from a dialog or menu. Keyboard focus must leave filter popups and song action menus naturally with Tab, return after dialogs, and return to the relevant setup control after managing sources, DJs, or provider keys without losing the draft. Opening a playlist name, source name, or new listening-room name form puts focus in its name field so typing works immediately. The Add to playlist form initially focuses the new-playlist name, and choosing Create a new playlist again focuses its newly shown name field. Editing values, changing source type, or background refreshes must not move focus back. Help and confirmation dialogs start on a safe non-destructive target. Escape, Cancel, Close and backdrop dismissal return focus to the opening control when it remains available. If a dialog removes its opening control, focus the current page heading. Keep long dialog titles compact so Close and keyboard actions remain reachable at the current acceptance baseline. Preserve the full accessible title. For DJ and source deletion, show the complete target name in wrapping body text so similarly named items remain distinguishable before confirmation. Give related source checkboxes a group name and keep interactive recovery controls outside live status/error announcements.

| M5 | I can find music and recover from a failed page | I am browsing a growing library or narrowing it by artist, album, genre or tag | Use Command-F to search, filter, select songs, open an album and return; Retry if the next page fails | Keep keyboard-focused rows/controls visible above the selection toolbar and player in songs, albums and playlists; quick arrow presses retain every move; show each song/album once across overlapping selected libraries, with unique totals and coherent pages; concurrent sort/filter reads of an unchanged selection do not falsely claim the library changed; Refresh rereads the server after a completed read, retains its focused action through busy/success/failure, ignores repeated activation while busy and leaves later Tab navigation in place; reset selection for a different search/filter; retain song selection and the same open album's track selection through ordinary page navigation; opening an album or playlist from its focused tile starts at the top on Back before reads finish; data updates leave later focus alone and sidebar return keeps its focus/scroll; Back closes the album, clears its selection and restores its tile focus even after a page detour; focused playlist Back restores that exact tile or the list heading when unavailable; opening from the list starts fresh, and library/account changes or restart clear temporary album selection; keep loaded songs/albums visible during a paging failure with explicit Retry; keyboard recovery focuses visible recovered results, the first new item after paging, or the heading of an empty page; failed retry retains its action, while later focus/navigation wins and background refreshes keep focus |
